characterization_methods.key_findings: The 0.012 wt.% C (baseline) plate shows coarse equiaxed single-phase grains with clean boundaries and only isolated dark dots/pits; no resolvable precipitates.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the microstructure of hot-rolled Fe-7Al-C plates with increasing carbon content.

characterization_methods.key_findings: Only Fe3Al reflections ((111), (220), (400), (422), (440)) are present in the 0.012 wt.% C baseline; no Fe3AlC0.5 peaks.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phases present in the Fe-7Al carbon-series alloys.
Determine room-temperature tensile properties of the hot-rolled carbon-series alloys.
Measure bulk hardness of the hot-rolled carbon-series alloys.

characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-7Al-.002C composition (wt.%): Al 6.86, Si 0.18, Mn 0.16, S 0.004, C 0.002.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine chemical composition of the AIMFC carbon-series alloys.

processing_steps.method: air induction melting with flux cover (AIMFC)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Forty-kilogram melts of five Fe-7Al-C alloys (Table IV) were prepared by AIMFC; the general AIMFC description mentions flux containing Al2O3, CaO, MgO and CaF2 and top pouring into split cast iron molds.
Hot-forged in a 1-tonne pneumatic forge hammer with die platens at room temperature; 24-mm-thick forged billets were then produced.
Samples were reheated after every six rolling passes under preheating conditions; final hot-rolled plate thickness was 12 mm.

structures.overall_structure: single-phase structure with no precipitates; coarse equiaxed grains

unmapped_findings: The carbon level of this baseline alloy is inconsistently reported: Table IV gives 0.002 wt.% C, Fig. 5 caption labels it 0.012 wt.% C, and the section text (b0061) refers to 0.02 C.

This sample is serial no. 1 (the carbon-free baseline) of the five Fe-7Al-C alloys prepared as 40-kg AIMFC melts; the Fig. 5 and Table V captions label the melting route 'AIM' although the section text (b0060) states the alloys were prepared by air induction melting with a flux cover (AIMFC).
